outcomeFindings.interpretation: The second untouched V1.9 holdout contained several new events but produced zero Primary selections. This supports the intended one-way nature of V1.9: a new event only opens a narrow audit path and does not force promotion.
A globally important new supply-policy event did not produce a durable base-horizon benchmark edge in the frozen A-share expression. V1.9 correctly kept it Research.
A new domestic supply-policy change did not justify Primary when the company/expectation bridge remained unresolved. The fresh-event label alone was not enough.

The Skill correctly identified the fresh environmental capacity shock and a direct earnings bridge, but blocked Primary because negative operating cash flow, large acquisition goodwill and financing/integration risks were material and not time-bounded. Strong later returns show a recall cost, but same-period hindsight cannot justify waiving company-risk controls.
A large macro-policy state change did not translate into a clean 60d company edge. Keeping the selected property expression Research was appropriate at the registered base horizon.

The frozen Shenzhen quality/growth basket strongly outperformed after Shenzhen Connect became operational, even though the event lacked a direct current earnings bridge. This may indicate a generic market-structure/ownership-base repricing channel that the current earnings-centric Skill does not model. It must not be converted into a Shenzhen-Connect-specific rule from this same-period result.

The frozen passenger-vehicle basket modestly outperformed despite No selection. Because the tax reset itself was not necessarily the causal driver of later OEM returns, this does not justify a sector-specific automotive rule. It is a reminder to separate policy-event causality from unrelated company fundamentals.

reasons: Three distinct new-event types in the same holdout—global supply coordination, domestic supply policy and environmental capacity disruption—were all evaluated through the same generic V1.9 contract and all remained no_route.
The only previously validated fresh-route Primary came from a different industry in 2017Q1, demonstrating that the route is not tied to a specific sector.
A strong later TiO2 return did not trigger a retrospective risk waiver.
Market-structure repricing is being treated as a generic missing causal channel, not a named-event exception.
prohibitedChanges: Do not add oil, coal, TiO2, auto, Shenzhen Connect or any named-stock rule.
Do not loosen adversarial company-risk gates because one risky Research name later rallied.
Do not add a generic market-structure route until it is defined independently of this outcome and validated on a future untouched window.
Do not merge dynamic re-underwrite into V1.9.

v19Assessment.firstUntouchedHoldout: 2017Q1: one fresh-route Primary strongly supported; new-event and continuation guardrails also supported.
v19Assessment.secondUntouchedHoldout: 2016Q4: zero Primary despite multiple new events; fresh-route precision/guardrail behavior supported.
v19Assessment.rationale: Two untouched windows support V1.9's generic discipline, but only one has produced a qualifying fresh-route Primary. A further untouched window is desirable before declaring the escalation route final.

nextValidationRequirement.action: Keep V1.9 unchanged and test another untouched earlier window.
nextValidationRequirement.preferredWindow: 2016Q3 if repository history confirms it is unused.
successCriteria: Do not require a Primary; zero-signal remains valid.
Any fresh-route Primary must arise from a frozen new event plus pre-event baseline and direct/quantified company path.
Continuation events remain excluded from fresh escalation.
If a market-structure/ownership repricing opportunity appears, record it as a diagnostic only; do not alter V1.9 within the same window.
